label: Straight
note: Owner-uploaded reference images. Authoritative for construction/appearance; NOT usable as the tech-pack illustration (not line art, or shows multiple options).

references.evidence: Photograph (248x248), styled flat-lay of FIVE different jacket sleeve cuffs fanned across each other - navy windowpane, olive, olive-grey, mid-blue and dark charcoal - plus a loose cluster of brown/red horn buttons bottom-right. Every cuff carries a column of 4 buttons, and on each one the worked buttonhole slits run PERPENDICULAR to that button column (dark bar-tacked slits emerging from each button toward the sleeve's back edge), which is the straight/horizontal traditional arrangement the label names. Two cuffs also show a contrast last buttonhole.
references.withheldReason: Styled flat-lay of FIVE different jackets. The buttonhole direction it shows is right, but the composition is a multi-garment still life; the single-cuff reference for this craft carries the same evidence without that hazard.

references.evidence: Sharpest of the four: photograph 382x274, tight close-up of a blue chalk-stripe jacket sleeve cuff resting on grey chalk-stripe cloth. Three of four tan horn buttons are visible in a column, and each has a hand-worked buttonhole running out across the sleeve from the button and finishing in a bar tack; the lowest buttonhole is fully open and clearly legible as a slit cut across the sleeve, perpendicular to the button column - straight/horizontal, not slanted along the sleeve and not vertical. The cuff is turned open so a rust-orange lining and the finished cuff hem also show.
